cases.name: basic::test_always_comb_read_before_write_uses_previous_value
cases.note: In `always_comb begin c = b; b = a; end`, `b` is written in the block so it is not in the sensitivity list (9.2.2.2.1) and `c` takes `b`'s previous value. Under the two-state contract `b` starts 0, but xezim leaves the comb-only variable `b` (and the never-yet-written input `i_a`) at X, so the first check sees c = X instead of 0. With `= '0` initializers added to `b` and `i_a` in a copy the case passes.

cases.name: basic::test_comb_function_call_expression_output_is_guarded_by_ternary
cases.note: always_comb { q_output = d; q_return = sel ? f(d, q_output) : 8'd7; } with sel=0, d=10: the false condition selects 8'd7, so f must not run and q_output stays 10. xezim runs f in the unselected arm and its output argument sets q_output to 11 (0xb). Same statement in an initial block is correct in xezim; Verilator gives q=10.

cases.name: basic::test_comb_function_call_expression_output_respects_short_circuit
cases.note: always_comb sets and_output = 0 then and_result = 1'b0 && f(d, and_output); the right operand of && is short-circuited, so f's output argument must not write and_output. xezim executes f, so and_output becomes d+1 = 0xb instead of 0.

cases.name: basic::test_comb_function_condition_output_is_guarded_after_early_return
cases.note: With sel=1, outer() returns early without reaching inner(x, y), so its output formal y is never written. It must still be copied out to q_output (two-state contract: 0; LRM four-state: x). xezim skips the copy-out of an output formal that is written only through a nested call that was not reached, so q_output keeps 7. Once this is fixed, xezim's x (the automatic logic default) against the suite's 0 would be a two-state-init difference.

cases.name: basic::test_comb_value_system_function_after_dynamic_break_stays_inactive
cases.note: The loop body runs the statement `$unsigned(f(d, q_output));`. With stop=0, count=2 and d=10, f must run and set q_output to 11. xezim never evaluates the argument of a system function used as a statement, so q_output stays 0. The stop=1 assertion passes only because nothing should run there.

cases.name: basic::test_comb_value_system_function_statement_applies_argument_outputs

cases.name: operators::simulates_systemverilog_packed_multidimensional_selects

cases.name: operators::simulates_systemverilog_selected_lvalue_assignments
cases.note: Only z[2] and z[0] are written by the always_comb; z[7:3] and z[1] are never written and stay X under xezim (got 0xx), 0 under the two-state contract (expected 0x5). cases.name: operators::simulates_systemverilog_selected_lvalue_ff_intermediate

cases.name: operators::unknown_logical_operand_evaluates_effectful_right_operand

cases.name: operators::wide_arithmetic_shift_preserves_unknown_sign

cases.name: packed_structs::packed_struct_alias_packed_dimensions

cases.name: packed_structs::packed_struct_bounds_and_type_queries

cases.name: packed_structs::packed_struct_layout_and_nested_fields

Icarus sign-extends. This is not bug E (no input port is involved; the field is read inside the module).

cases.name: packed_structs::packed_struct_whole_value_signedness

cases.name: procedural::aggregate_parameters_are_constant_tables

cases.name: procedural::concatenated_targets_fix_their_positions_first

cases.name: procedural::select_index_calls_run_as_written
cases.note: In always_ff, `bits[c ? tick(calls, calls) : 2'd3] = 1'b1` with c=0 still calls tick in the unselected arm, so ff_count = 4 instead of 3. The same statement in initial/always_comb is correct (mux_count passes).

cases.name: procedural::static_function_result_keeps_value_between_calls
cases.note: `function static bit [15:0] saved` writes its result only when write_value=1; called from always_ff with update=0 after storing 23, xezim returns 0 instead of 23 (0x17). From an initial procedure the result is retained (23,23).

cases.name: random_plusargs::dist_uniform_converts_wide_and_signed_seeds_to_int_formals

cases.name: random_plusargs::dist_uniform_reference_sequence
cases.note: $dist_uniform(seed=17,-17,23) must give -17 and seed 1174174 per Annex N; xezim gives 0 and 4596240 (and all later values differ). Icarus reproduces the expected sequence.

cases.name: real_math::constant_functions

cases.name: review_regressions::body_parameters_are_local_with_a_parameter_port_list
cases.note: With a parameter_port_list, the body `parameter P` is a localparam and the #(.P(205)) override in parameters.sv must be rejected. xezim enforces this only when the module and the overriding instance are in one file; with the instance in a separate file it elaborates and applies the override (p=cf). Icarus and Verilator reject.

cases.name: review_regressions::default_pattern_fills_each_element_of_unpacked_subarrays
cases.note: c = '{default: b} with int c[2][2] and int b[2] must assign b to each subarray (subarray type matches the value's type), so z00 = d = 0x20. xezim leaves all elements 0. The y00..y11 asserts before it pass; the y part is fine.

cases.name: review_regressions::folds_compound_four_state_case_labels
cases.note: The only failing item is the label (1'bx ? 1'bz : 1'bz) when s=z (expected ~a, xezim keeps the old y=0). xezim folds the label to x per Table 11-20 (z,z -> x); the suite (and Icarus) read it as z because both operands are identical. 11.4.11 applies Table 11-20 only when the operands are 'not logically equivalent', and does not say whether z and z are logically equivalent (z==z is x), while the table explicitly lists z/z -> x.

cases.name: review_regressions::int_parameters_are_signed_in_comparisons_and_loop_bounds
cases.note: Port `input int lo` connected to unsigned `logic [31:0] i_lo` = 0xfffffffe is treated as unsigned, so lo < S (S=2) is false (lt_s expected 1, got 0). Changing the testbench actual to `logic signed [31:0] i_lo` makes the whole case pass.

cases.name: review_regressions::lowers_parameter_casts_in_conditional_generate
cases.note: select_t'(4) with select_t = logic [1:0] (W=2) is 2'b00, so the nested generate takes the `selected` branch and comb_y follows data. xezim's constant evaluation ignores the typedef cast width (4 -> true) and elaborates `disabled` (comb_y=0). Replacing select_t'(4) by 1'b0 makes the case pass.

cases.name: review_regressions::normalizes_function_parameter_cast_dimensions
cases.note: All six functions take formals with ranges not based at 0 ([8:1], [1:8], typedef [W'(8):W'(1)]) and are called from always_comb; with data=0x40 each should return data[6]=1 (y=0x3f). xezim, inside always_comb/always @*/assign, indexes the formal as if it were [7:0] (x[7] reads d[7]), giving y=0; the same call from an initial block is right.

cases.name: review_regressions::preserves_four_state_arithmetic_case_constants
cases.note: Only y11 fails: case (+(2'b1z)) with label 2'bxx. Unary plus is an arithmetic operator, so any x/z operand bit makes the whole result x (xx). xezim (and Icarus) return 2'b1z unchanged, so the label does not match and y11 stays X. Replacing that selector by 2'bxx makes the case pass.

cases.name: review_regressions::preserves_four_state_equality_case_selectors
cases.note: Only y8 fails: case ((1'bx == 1'bx) ? 1'bz : 1'bz) with label 1'bz. The condition is x; xezim combines z and z per Table 11-20 into x, so the label 1'bz does not match (y8=X); the suite and Icarus treat identical operands as 'logically equivalent' and yield z. cases.name: review_regressions::preserves_four_state_shift_and_bit_select_constants
cases.note: Only y1 fails: case (4'sbz101 >>> 2) with the unsigned label 4'b00z1. 12.5 makes all case expressions unsigned when any is unsigned, so >>> is a logical shift giving 00z1. xezim evaluates the case expression signed (zzz1), so it does not match and y1 stays X. cases.name: review_regressions::preserves_use_site_dimensions_in_function_alias_types
cases.note: xezim rejects the valid non-ANSI formal `input nibble_t [2:1] x;` with 'Undeclared identifier x' (build.log line 19). With that declaration rewritten as `input logic [2:1][3:0] x;` it builds, then high_y = high(data) with formal nibble_t [2:1] reads x (expected 0xa, got x), which is sv_rest-X63 (a formal range not based at 0, called from always_comb).

cases.name: review_regressions::resolves_generate_local_alias_casts_for_all_processes
cases.note: localparam S = select_t'(4) (select_t = logic [1:0]) must be 2'b00, so `if (S)` selects `selected` and comb_y follows data. xezim evaluates S=4 (32 bits), picks `disabled`, comb_y=0. Replacing select_t'(4) by 1'b0 makes the case pass.

cases.name: scan::sscanf_integral_fields_and_failure_counts
cases.note: ' 12,99 ffQ' with '%2d,%*d %h%c' gives n=1 (a=12, b=c=0) in xezim: scanning stops after the suppressed %*d (expected n=3, b=255, c=81). Also $sscanf('', '%d', keep) returns 0 instead of EOF -1 (sv_rest-X16).

cases.name: scan::sscanf_radix_unknowns_and_unknown_input
cases.note: xezim does not accept x/z digits: '1z' with %h gives 8'h01 (expected 8'h1z), 'x' with %d and 'z' with %b return 0 (expected 1, xx/zz). An unknown str (32'hx) returns 0 instead of EOF -1 (sv_rest-X16).

cases.name: scan::sscanf_real_fields_width_and_suppression
cases.note: '3.5e1,2.25' with '%*g,%f' returns 0 and leaves b unchanged in xezim (expected 1, 2.25): the suppressed conversion stops the scan. $sscanf('', '%f', keep) returns 0 instead of EOF -1 (sv_rest-X16).

cases.name: string::casts_from_integral_values
cases.note: s = "x\0y" must drop the \0 (len 2, 'xy'); xezim keeps the NUL (len 3, prints 'x y'). The string'(word) cast line matches.

cases.name: synthesizable::instance_arrays_reject_a_fill_literal_tie_off
cases.note: Pass u[1:0](.b('0)) on an 8-bit port: 23.3.3.5 requires the connection to match one instance port or all instances, and 5.7.1 gives '0 a width of 1 bit only 'in a self-determined context'. The suite reads the instance-array connection size as self-determined (1 bit -> error, Verilator agrees); xezim treats '0 as filling the port it connects to, the way it does for a single instance (23.3.3.2), and the LRM does not say which context applies to the 23.3.3.5 size check.

cases.name: synthesizable::instance_arrays_reject_an_unsized_constant_tie_off
cases.note: The unsized constant 0 is 32 bits, neither the 8-bit port nor the 16 bits of both instances, which 23.3.3.5 calls an error ('Too many or too few bits'). xezim only warns about a width mismatch and elaborates. Icarus and Verilator reject.

cases.name: synthesizable::named_calls_in_constant_contexts
cases.note: In the non-top module Top, f(.b(2), .a(3)) used as a constant (localparam and packed dimension) evaluates to 0, so word_value is [-1:0] and y = 0x1 instead of 0x80000001. With the calls rewritten positionally the y/ok asserts pass, and then query fails (0x11 instead of 0x10) because $unpacked_dimensions(f(3)) returns 1 (sv_rest-X71).

cases.name: synthesizable::named_calls_preserve_defaults_and_declaration_scope
cases.note: localparam N = f(.b(3)) (a = default 7) must be 73 = 0x49; xezim's constant evaluation of the named call gives 0 (constant_value got 0x0). The runtime named calls y/z/positional/q pass; with N written as f(7, 3) the whole case passes.

cases.name: synthesizable::named_calls_respect_generate_signatures
cases.note: The module-level call f(.a(x)) must call the module's f (a+1 = 4), but xezim binds it to the f declared in generate block `scoped` (b+10, with b unbound -> 10 = 0xa). After renaming the inner function, outer_y is still wrong (1) because a continuous assignment whose operand is only a named argument does not re-evaluate when x changes (sv_rest-X70).

cases.name: synthesizable::type_parameter_bindings_preserve_alias_dimensions
cases.note: Child #(.T(nibble_t [N-1:0])) should make T 8 bits; xezim ignores this override and uses the default logic signed [3:0] (t_bits=4). With T written as logic signed [N-1:0][3:0], u_bits still fails (8 instead of 16) because the default U = T [1:0] also drops its packed dimensions. Both come from one defect: a type identifier followed by packed dimensions in a type parameter.

cases.name: synthesizable::type_parameter_bindings_use_caller_scope
cases.note: In Child #(.T(logic signed [W-1:0])), W must resolve to Top's W=8, but xezim uses Child's own parameter W=2 (literal_width got 2). With W-1 replaced by 7, literal_negative still fails because a signed port U connected to unsigned `a` acts unsigned (bug E). Feeding a signed copy of a as well makes the case pass.

cases.name: synthesizable::type_parameters_are_bound_by_instantiations
cases.note: Neg #(.T(logic signed [7:0])) has a signed input port connected to the unsigned part-select a[7:0], and xezim treats it as unsigned (signed_neg expected 1 for 0x80, got 0). Connecting a `logic signed [7:0]` copy of a[7:0] makes the case pass. Even a $signed(a[7:0]) actual stays unsigned under xezim.

cases.name: system_functions::array_queries_handle_runtime_dimensions
cases.note: For logic [7:4] mem [2:5] the runtime dimension argument 0, 3, 0x08000001, -1 and all-x must give 'x for $left/$right/$low/$high/$increment; xezim returns numbers instead (d=0 acts as dimension 1: l=2 r=5; d=3 gives l=3 r=0). The in-range dimensions 1 and 2 pass.

cases.name: system_functions::array_queries_preserve_bounds_and_dimensions
cases.note: selected = $left(mem[0]) + $right(mem[0][7]) + $dimensions(mem[0][7]) must be 8+3+2=13; xezim gives 7 (6+0+1): queries on selects ignore the selected element's type (X1). parameter_value must be 13+9+1=23; in the instantiated Top xezim computes the localparam P as 23 and BL=$left(BOUND) as 0, giving 24 (X4); as the root module P=13, BL=9.

cases.name: system_functions::bit_vector_predicates_in_constant_expressions
cases.note: `localparam U = $isunknown(256'hx)` evaluates to 0 in xezim's constant evaluator (runtime $isunknown gives 1), so the generate condition fails and result is 0 instead of 0xa5. H and Z and the runtime `literals` are correct. The constant evaluator drops x/z bits, which is the same defect as the $countbits cases.

cases.name: system_functions::character_formats_preserve_non_utf8_bytes
cases.note: Only the `%3s` field of 8'hfe differs: expected two pad spaces then byte 0xfe (`20 20 fe`), xezim writes one space (`20 fe`). xezim measures the field width by the UTF-8 encoded length of the character (0xfe -> 2 bytes) while emitting the raw byte; %3s of 8'h41 pads correctly. 21.2.1.7 makes each 8 bits one character and 21.2.1.2 pads strings to the field width with leading spaces.

cases.name: system_functions::countbits_in_constant_expressions
cases.note: In constant context xezim gets X=$countbits(MIXED,'x)=5, Z=5 and K=$countbits(MIXED,'0,'1)=8, where 2, 2 and 4 are expected for MIXED=8'b10xz_11xz. x/z are turned into 0 in both the operand and the control bits, so the generate condition fails and result is 0 instead of 520. The same calls evaluated at runtime are correct (t1..t8 all match), and Icarus and Verilator give 2/2/4.

cases.name: system_functions::countbits_in_parameter_specializations_and_generate_scopes
cases.note: Only `scoped` fails (expected 2, got -1). The generate condition `$countbits(MIXED,'x,'z) == 4` is constant-evaluated with x/z turned into 0 (it counts the five 0 bits instead of 4), so the else branch is taken. The runtime counts (c_original=4, extended=5, via_function=4) are correct.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_counts_declared_arrays
cases.note: Only scalar = $dimensions(logic s) differs: suite expects 0, xezim returns 1 (Icarus and Verilator return 0); all array, atom and logic [0:0] counts pass. Reading A (suite, Icarus 13, Verilator 5.052): a scalar bit/logic has no packed dimension; 20.7 gives a [n-1:0] dimension only to the predefined-width integer types, and with $dimensions=1 the 20.7 rule that $left etc. return 'x when $dimensions is 0 would leave scalar bounds undefined. Reading B (xezim): 6.11.1 says the Table 6-8 integer types (which include bit and logic) are simple bit vector types, so a scalar is a 'nonarray type equivalent to a simple bit vector type' and 20.7 gives 1.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_is_independent_of_unknown_values
cases.note: parameter_value = $dimensions(P) for localparam logic [1:0][3:0] P must be 2 and the generate branch on N==2 must give 0x1234; in the instantiated Top xezim evaluates the localparam query to 0, so both fail (X4; the x/z bits are irrelevant: P = 8'h00 also gives 0). scalar_value = $dimensions(a[0][0]) gets 1 vs expected 0 (select ignored, X1; the 0-vs-1 scalar rank is also the lrm_ambiguous scalar question).

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_preserves_one_bit_vectors
cases.note: Only scalar_rank = $dimensions(localparam logic SCALAR) and bit_cast_rank = $dimensions(scalar_t'(s)) with typedef bit scalar_t differ: suite expects 0, xezim 1; all one-bit vector forms (1'b0, {s}, '0, logic [0:0], 1'(s)) pass with 1. Both failing operands have scalar type. Reading A (suite, Icarus 13, Verilator 5.052): a scalar bit/logic has no packed dimension; 20.7 gives a [n-1:0] dimension only to the predefined-width integer types, and with $dimensions=1 the 20.7 rule that $left etc. return 'x when $dimensions is 0 would leave scalar bounds undefined. Reading B (xezim): 6.11.1 says the Table 6-8 integer types (which include bit and logic) are simple bit vector types, so a scalar is a 'nonarray type equivalent to a simple bit vector type' and 20.7 gives 1.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_preserves_selected_and_expression_types
cases.note: For a [1:0][3:0] and memory [0:1][0:2] of that type, $dimensions((a)) must be 2, a[1:0] 2, memory[index] 3, identity(a) (returns logic [1:0][3:0]) 2; xezim returns 1 for every non-identifier operand (parenthesized, slice, select, call, -a, ~a, a<<1). The -a/~a/a<<1 expectations of 2 rely on the operand type being preserved by unary/shift operators (11.8.1 leaves this loose), but the parenthesis/slice/select/call failures are unambiguous. scalar (a[i][0]) 1 vs 0 is also the scalar-rank question.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_resolves_imported_function_returns
cases.note: localparam N = $dimensions(f()) must be 2 for the imported/qualified package function returning logic [1:0][3:0] and 1 for Child's local logic [7:0] f(); xezim gives 0 for all three: queries in parameter initializers evaluate to 0 in instantiated modules (X4). At run time xezim would still give 1 for any call (X1).

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_resolves_package_array_constants
cases.note: Package localparams N = $dimensions(A) (A: logic [7:0] [0:1]) and ELEMENT = $dimensions(A[0]) must be 2 and 1; xezim evaluates both to 0 because array queries in package parameter initializers give 0 (PK=0 in the X4 repro, also with Top as root).

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_resolves_preceding_block_declarations
cases.note: In always_comb, logic [$dimensions(a):0] b with a: logic [7:0] [0:1] must be 3 bits; xezim makes it 2 bits ($dimensions(a) evaluated as 1 in a block-local declaration range), while the runtime first_rank/second_rank (2) pass.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_resolves_procedural_scopes
cases.note: task query(input logic [7:0] x [0:1]) must give $dimensions(x)*10 + $dimensions(local_array) = 2*10+4 = 24; xezim gives 44 because the always_comb also calls nested(), whose named block declares x [0:1][0:2][0:3], and the formal x resolves to that block-local x (rank 4). Removing the nested() call or calling from initial gives 24.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_resolves_types_and_constant_scopes
cases.note: In the instantiated Top: $dimensions(memory_t) (typedef pair_t memory_t [0:2][0:3]) 2 vs 4, Child's localparam N = $dimensions(T) 0 vs 2/1, and every dependent value (bits_value ranges 1 vs 7/3, generate condition N==2 so scoped -1 and generated 0) fail from X4. cast_shape pair_t'(8'h5a) 1 vs 2 and real_literal 1 vs 0 are X1, string_type $dimensions(string) 0 vs 1 is X2, local_shape 13 vs 23 is X7 (formal x resolves to the module's logic [7:0] x); scalar_parameter 1 vs 0 is the ambiguous scalar rank.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_signing_conversions_are_vectors
cases.note: Only scalar_rank = $dimensions(input logic s) differs (expected 0, xezim 1); all signing conversions (expected 1) and the packed operand (2) pass. Reading A (suite, Icarus 13, Verilator 5.052): a scalar bit/logic has no packed dimension; 20.7 gives a [n-1:0] dimension only to the predefined-width integer types, and with $dimensions=1 the 20.7 rule that $left etc. return 'x when $dimensions is 0 would leave scalar bounds undefined. Reading B (xezim): 6.11.1 says the Table 6-8 integer types (which include bit and logic) are simple bit vector types, so a scalar is a 'nonarray type equivalent to a simple bit vector type' and 20.7 gives 1.

cases.name: system_functions::dimensions_types_function_pattern_arguments
cases.note: localparam N = $dimensions(f('{8'h1, 8'h2})) with f returning logic [7:0] must be 1; xezim evaluates it to 0 in the instantiated Top (array queries in parameter initializers give 0, X4). runtime_rank passes (xezim's constant 1 for calls happens to match).

cases.name: system_functions::display_arguments_are_sized_as_ieee_specifies
cases.note: Only the last field of line 3 differs: `%d` of `input logic signed [7:0] s` = -2 prints `254` instead of `  -2`. The testbench actual `i_s` is unsigned `logic [7:0]`, and xezim takes the port's signedness from the actual (known bug E). With `i_s` declared `logic signed [7:0]` in a copy, the whole output matches the expectation.

cases.name: system_functions::display_expressions_propagate_operand_widths
cases.note: Expected `ffffffff -1 ...`, xezim prints `ff 255 ...`: `sa + 1` with `input logic signed [7:0] sa` = 0xfe is evaluated unsigned (8-bit 0xff, 255) because the tb actual `i_sa` is unsigned (bug E). The remaining five fields already match. With `i_sa` declared signed in a copy the output is exactly `ffffffff -1 f7 6d 8031 fb 84`.

cases.name: system_functions::display_field_flags
cases.note: The two `%05d` fields differ: suite expects `[00042]` (C-style zero flag, as Icarus does), xezim prints `[   42]`; every `-` (left-justify) field already matches. IEEE 1800-2023 defines no format flags: 21.2.1.2 only allows a non-negative decimal field width (05 = 5) and says decimal values are padded with leading spaces, so xezim's output is the LRM result. The case itself is labelled as Icarus/Verilator flag compatibility; the zero-pad expectation is a tool extension, not an LRM requirement, and should be tagged as such rather than counted against xezim.

cases.name: system_functions::isunbounded_binds_procedural_aliases_in_declaration_order
cases.note: Each block declares localparam int U = $, COPY = U, AGAIN = COPY, so all three $isunbounded must be 1 (7). In the initial block and the always_ff xezim gives 3'b100 (only U), and via_function (query() in a continuous assignment) gives 0 (constant-folded call, X41).

cases.name: system_functions::isunbounded_generate_guards_preserve_short_circuit_bounds
cases.note: In generate block g with localparam int P = $, logic [($isunbounded(P) || P == 0):0] b must be 2 bits; xezim makes it 1 bit because $isunbounded evaluates to 0 in constant expressions (packed range here). and_bits (1) passes.

cases.name: system_functions::isunbounded_preserves_lexical_scopes_and_short_circuits

cases.name: system_functions::printtimescale_displays_unit_and_global_precision

cases.name: system_functions::random_follows_annex_n_and_updates_its_seed
cases.note: With start=0 Annex N's rtl_dist_uniform(seed, LONG_MIN, LONG_MAX) gives 303379748 and leaves seed=-1844104698 (Icarus 13 and a C transcription of N.2 agree); xezim returns 1359758873 and writes the same value back into the seed (comb_seed=0x510c4619). cases.name: system_functions::random_without_a_seed_continues_its_stream
cases.note: Expected first unseeded draws 303379748 -1064739199 (the zero-seed Annex N stream); xezim prints -375392153 942667852 then 1830663020 -1264564434. cases.name: system_functions::scope_randomize_obeys_control_flow_and_statement_order

cases.name: system_functions::timescale_queries_accept_directives_before_unit_declarations

cases.name: system_functions::timescale_queries_accept_separate_initial_declarations

cases.name: system_functions::unpacked_dimensions_accepts_defaulted_function_arguments

cases.note: Package localparam N = $unpacked_dimensions(A) for A: logic [7:0] [0:1] must be 1; xezim evaluates it to 0 (array queries in package parameter initializers give 0). ELEMENT passes (0).

cases.name: system_functions::unpacked_dimensions_selects_integral_atoms
cases.note: Selects of int i (i[index], i[index +: 3]) and a[0][3] of int a [0:1] have no unpacked dimension, so 0 is required; xezim returns 1 for each select (runtime_rank, slice_rank, array_rank); constant_rank passes.

cases.name: system_functions::unpacked_dimensions_types_function_pattern_arguments

cases.name: system_functions::unpacked_dimensions_validates_writable_function_arguments
cases.note: rank = $unpacked_dimensions(f(a, a)) of an int-returning function must be 0; xezim returns 1; untouched (7) and the no-output check pass, so the call is not executed.

cases.name: system_functions::urandom_comb_executes_in_statement_order
cases.note: The case reseeds with $urandom(working_seed) and expects the next draw() to replay `second`. xezim's $urandom(seed) returns a seed-determined value but does not reseed the calling thread's RNG, so ok=0 for all 4 checks. A copy that replaces each `x = $urandom(s)` with `process::self().srandom(s); x = $urandom` passes, so seeding is the only defect (the short-circuited $urandom operands in always_comb are not evaluated).

cases.name: system_functions::urandom_extends_signed_seed_values
cases.note: For bits=128..255, $urandom(narrow) with logic signed [7:0] narrow differs from $urandom(int'(narrow)), so ff_ok and comb_ok are 0 (256 failing asserts; bits 0..127 pass). The seed formal is `int seed`, and passing -128 to it must sign-extend. A copy that passes int'(narrow) explicitly passes all 512 asserts.

cases.name: system_functions::urandom_keeps_process_and_instance_streams_independent
cases.note: After both Generator instances reseed with 123, a draws alone and then b draws alone, and b must produce the value a drew. xezim gives same=0 in all 8 iterations because all processes share one $urandom stream: another process's earlier draw changes a thread's next value (repro: x=3919575143 alone vs 942667852 when a later-declared process also draws). This still fails after the reseed is replaced with process::self().srandom(123), so X22 alone does not explain it.

cases.name: system_functions::urandom_reseeds_and_shares_the_calling_process_stream
cases.note: Three bugs combine here. ok=0: $urandom(seed) does not reseed the thread, so replay_b/replay_c differ from b/c (X22), and `width <= $bits($urandom())` makes an extra draw (X25). unchanged=0: xezim writes the new seed back into the `seed` input (X21). A copy with srandom-based reseeding, a constant width, and a temporary seed variable passes all 20 asserts.

cases.name: system_functions::urandom_respects_short_circuits_and_evaluates_indices_once
cases.note: The second $urandom(42) does not replay the thread stream (X22). In the always_ff body, xezim also evaluates the short-circuited operands of `0 && $urandom`, `1 || $urandom` and `1 ? 0 : $urandom` (X26): with the reseed worked around, actual=938043164 instead of third=1478287871. The index select draws only once. A copy with srandom reseeding and the three short-circuit lines removed passes.

cases.name: system_functions::urandom_select_keeps_distinct_source_calls
cases.note: check_calls() reseeds with $urandom(seed) (seed=17) and expects the next draws to replay a, b and third. xezim does not reseed the thread RNG, so ff_ok and comb_ok are 0. With srandom-based reseeding in a copy, all 4 asserts pass, which shows that `($urandom() + $urandom())` in the select index is evaluated correctly.

cases.name: timing::always_star_timed_task_calls_wait_on_folded_branch_reads
cases.note: y stays 0 at time 3 (expected 1): xezim does not wake always @* begin if (0) delayed(); delayed(b); end when a, read only by the default of delayed's omitted argument, changes at 2. 9.4.2.2 builds @* from the nets and variables 'that appear in the statement' (with 'read by the statement' in its first paragraph). The variable a appears only in the declaration of an omitted argument's default (13.5.3), not in the statement. Reading 1 (the suite's, also in limitations.json): a default evaluated for the call is read by the statement, so a change of a wakes the process. Reading 2: only identifiers written in the statement count, the same way reads inside a called function's body do not, so a is not in the list and xezim's y=0 conforms. xezim does include syntactic reads of a constant-false branch (probe: if (0) d2(a) wakes on a), so only the default-argument question decides this case.

cases.name: timing::always_star_timed_task_calls_wait_on_nested_call_defaults
cases.note: y stays 0 at time 3 (expected 5): always @* delayed(pick()) is not woken by a change of a, read only by pick's default argument. 9.4.2.2 builds @* from the nets and variables 'that appear in the statement' (with 'read by the statement' in its first paragraph). The variable a appears only in the declaration of an omitted argument's default (13.5.3), not in the statement. Reading 1 (the suite's, also in limitations.json): a default evaluated for the call is read by the statement, so a change of a wakes the process. Reading 2: only identifiers written in the statement count, the same way reads inside a called function's body do not, so a is not in the list and xezim's y=0 conforms. xezim does include syntactic reads of a constant-false branch (probe: if (0) d2(a) wakes on a), so only the default-argument question decides this case. A side finding: standalone, xezim runs this always @* at time 0 and then stalls at time 1 (zero-delay livelock), recorded as sv_hier-X32. In the suite run it did not stall, and the stall does not change this case's verdict.

cases.name: timing::any_change_waits_wake_on_every_value_change
cases.note: xezim prints the expected lines in a different order: at t=3 'either' before 'data=7'. Both processes ('@(data)' and '@(flag, data)') are woken by the same update of data, and 4.7 lets events be taken off the Active region in any order. So the expected text 'data=7\neither\n...' fixes an order the LRM leaves nondeterministic. xezim's output has the same set of lines per time step, so the expectation, not xezim, is at fault. Not a settle artifact: the case uses run_to_finish.

cases.name: timing::blocking_ff_woken_waiters_sample_before_continuations
cases.note: a=0 and b=0 at time 1 (expected 1, 1): @(posedge (go & enable)) is never woken when Child's always_ff @(posedge clk) go = 1 (blocking) raises go. A standalone repro without the suite testbench fails the same way: plain always @(posedge clk) go = 1 also fails, a nonblocking write or a write from an initial block works, and adding any process waiting directly on @(go) makes the expression waiter wake. Not a settle artifact.

cases.name: timing::blocking_write_waiters_rearm_before_nonblocking_updates
cases.note: Output n=1 r=1 (expected n=3 r=3). always @(posedge clk) begin y = 1; y <= 0; y <= 1; end: the two NBAs must apply 0 then 1 in order (4.6 b), each an update event that wakes @(y)/@(posedge y). xezim coalesces them to the final value, so only the first blocking 0->1 is seen. The variable is also written by both blocking and nonblocking assignments, the X40 pattern. Standalone repro, no settle involved (run_to_finish).

cases.name: timing::constant_variable_initializers_do_not_invent_clock_edges
cases.note: function_seen=1 and copy_seen=1 at time 0 (expected 0): the declaration initializers bit function_clock = high_value() and bit copied_clock = literal_clock produce a posedge that wakes always_ff @(posedge ...). Static declaration initialization happens before any initial or always procedure starts (6.8, 10.5), so no edge exists. Literal and parameter initializers are handled correctly. Reproduced standalone without the settler.

cases.name: timing::cross_file_package_initializers_keep_static_clock_baseline
cases.note: qualified=1 and imported=1 at times 0 and 1 (expected 0): bit clk = P::high_value() (a package function) as a declaration initializer gives an edge at time 0 that runs always @(posedge clk) q++. A single-file standalone probe gives q=1 as well, so this is X35, not a cross-file or settle effect.

cases.name: timing::direct_reads_settle_waiting_processes
cases.note: seen=1 (expected 2). The design does wait (go); seen = 1; #0; seen = 2. The settle after the write lets the settler program ack while the design's #0 continuation (Inactive region) is still pending, which 4.5 forbids: Reactive runs only when [Active ... Post-Observed] is empty. The settle mechanism triggers this, but the defect is xezim's: the standalone repro (no suite code) shows the program running before the #0 continuation once a program has already run in that time step. Without the earlier settle, xezim orders it correctly. Icarus agrees with xezim but treats program blocks as modules.

cases.name: timing::intermediate_combinational_writes_keep_other_drivers
cases.note: Output n=1 m=2 (expected n=2 m=3). While a=1, each change of b re-runs always_comb y[3:0] = 0; if (a) y[3:0] = 1;, which pulses y 0xa1 -> 0xa0 -> 0xa1. The intermediate value change is an update event that must wake @(y) (4.3, 4.5), but xezim drops waiter wakeups from intermediate blocking writes within one process activation. Not settle-related (run_to_finish).

cases.name: timing::intermediate_combinational_writes_wake_waiters
cases.note: Output comb=1 star=1 (expected 3, 3): the 1 -> 0 -> 1 rewrites of y1/y2 inside always_comb / always @* on each change of b do not wake @(y1)/@(y2). Each intermediate change is an update event (4.3, 4.5). The repro shows the same with a plain always @(b) (xezim n=0, Icarus n=2).

cases.name: timing::intermediate_edge_process_writes_wake_waiters
cases.note: Output blk=1 nba=1 const=1 rise=1 fall=0 (expected 3 3 3 3 2). blk/const/fall come from the blocking pulses y3 = 0; y3 = 1 and y5 = 0; y5 = 1 not waking waiters (X36). nba/rise come from y4 <= 0; y4 <= 1 being coalesced so the 1->0->1 NBA updates are not seen (X34). Both reproduce standalone; no settle involved.

cases.name: timing::negative_real_delays_wait_their_twos_complement
cases.note: woke=1 (expected 0): #r with real r = -1.5 resumes immediately. 9.4.1 interprets a negative delay as a two's-complement unsigned time (about 2^64 steps), so the wakeup is far after the #10 $finish. Integer #(-1) behaves the same in xezim (woke_int=1); Icarus gives 0 for both.

cases.name: timing::negative_repeat_counts_do_not_run_the_body
cases.note: dynamic_count=3 and positive_count=0 (expected 0, 2): Top's input integer n receives 0xfffffffe from the testbench's unsigned logic [31:0] i_n. xezim takes the port's signedness from the actual, so n is 4294967294 instead of -2 and repeat(n) loops (12.7.2 treats a negative count as zero). Declaring i_n as integer in a copy of testbench.sv makes the case pass.
